episodes.212563: Mid level moisture pulled up ahead of an upper level disturbance over the western U.S. combined with intense daytime heating resulted in the development of high based showers and thunderstorms across west central New Mexico midday June 8th moving northeast across central New Mexico during the late afternoon and early evening hours. Little to no rainfall from these high based showers and thunderstorms reached the ground and instead resulted in erratic wind gusts and areas of blowing dust. Some of these virga showers and dry thunderstorms resulted in severe wind gusts at a personal weather station in western Albuquerque and at the Santa Fe Municipal Airport. The disturbance moved across the state on June 9th resulting in high based showers and storms across central New Mexico and wetter strong to severe storms across eastern New Mexico due to higher low level moisture across this part of the state. Severe wind gusts were observed at the Wild Rivers RAWS near Questa and at Conchas Lake State Park. Finally, very dry and gusty winds were observed across far western New Mexico with a brief high wind gust at Gallup Municipal Airport during the afternoon hours June 9th.
episodes.212586: Localized heavy rainfall over downtown Auburn, up to 2.5-3 inches, led to numerous roadways becoming flooded, with a few stranded vehicles, in the area of Auburn University and Town Creek.
episodes.212590: A mesoscale convective system (MCS) developed and tracked southeast through Middle Tennessee during the afternoon of June 9, 2026. With abnormally high amounts of atmospheric moisture, these thunderstorms were able to produce very heavy rainfall with rain amounts of five to seven inches reported across portions of Sumner and Robertson counties. This caused flash flooding for these areas, particularly in low-lying areas and those along area creeks. This MCS also produced severe thunderstorm winds which downed several trees and caused other minor damage before it weakened across southern Middle Tennessee.
episodes.212595: During the 9th evening, a moist and unstable airmass across central Indiana interacted with an approaching upper-level disturbance resulting in severe thunderstorms. Thunderstorms initially developed in western and northwestern central Indiana after 6:00 PM EST before organizing into line segments that tracked eastward across the region through the late evening and overnight hours.||Strong straight-line wind gusts were produced by the severe thunderstorms. Peak measured wind gusts reached 61 mph at the Purdue University Airport in Tippecanoe County and 63 mph at the Indianapolis Regional Airport in Hancock County. The severe winds caused broad impacts across Tippecanoe, Vigo, Clay, Morgan, Hendricks, Hancock, and Johnson counties, primarily consisting of downed trees, large tree limbs, and localized power line damage that created temporary roadway obstructions.||Repeated convective activity and heavy rainfall totals between 2.5 and 4 inches subsequently impacted eastern portions of the area during the early morning hours of June 10. This heavy rain led to localized flash flooding across roadways in Decatur County, though no building inundation or water rescues were reported before floodwaters receded. This severe weather event would be the second of many for the month which would eventually define a formal disaster period from June 6th to the 18th which was declared by the governor of Indiana.
episodes.212597: Northeast Kansas continued to endure one of its worst stretches of severe storms in recent memory with another high impact wind and flood event.  A cluster of storms developed in north central Kansas and evolved into a bow echo.  The storms produced destructive winds in excess of 100 mph across parts of Ottawa county with a swath of winds of 75-95 mph causing damage from Dickinson county east along I-70 into Douglas County including the city of Topeka.  Widespread damage occurred due to the winds.  Torrential flooding rains of 2-3 inches per hour also plagued the area and produced damaging flooding across many areas during the night.   Two to six inches of rain fell over already saturated grounds causing the flooding.  There were also two documented tornadoes one in Dickinson county and a small tornado in Douglas County on the north side of the city of Lawrence.
episodes.212636: A cluster of storms initially generated hail mainly to the size of quarters across portions of central South Dakota, then organized into a line and increased speed. This resulted in high winds across northeast South Dakota during the late evening and early overnight hours. A peak wind gust of 90 mph was recorded by the South Dakota Department of Transportation (SDDOT) mesonet station 4 miles north of Altamont, with a 78 mph wind gust recorded on a personal weather station 9 miles northwest of Aberdeen, 77 mph on a personal weather station in Faulkton and a 74 mph gust at the SDDOT station near Ree Heights (Hand County). ||Intermittent wind damage was reported across much of northeast South Dakota, with reports of peeled roofs and lost tiles, blown in garages and trees down. In the city of Aberdeen and surrounding area, several of these trees landed on vehicles. The Aberdeen City Forester reported the cost for just tree cleanup on city property (including boulevards) topped out at $14,585. ||Six miles south of Goodwin, multiple irrigation pivots were twisted by intense winds. Major power outages affected 5,849 customers in Brown County, 1,106 in Hamlin County, and 64 in Deuel County.
episodes.212643: A few strong to severe thunderstorms moved east into far northwest Kansas during the late evening hours on the 8th. Up to golfball sized hail occurred in Sherman county. Additionally, a church north of St. Francis completely burned after being struck by lightning by one of the thunderstorms.
episodes.212740: Supercell thunderstorms rolled across the Denver Metro area mid afternoon on June 8th producing up to golf ball sized hail. Isolate severe wind gusts were recorded as well. As the storms progressed east of the Denver their intensity increase. A supercell thunderstorm continued to track eastward, stay south of I-70. Farther north, thunderstorms organized into a broken line, producing wind gusts of 55 to 70 mph across far northeast Colorado.
episodes.212880: Rich moisture advected into the region ahead of a dryline positioned across the south-central Texas Panhandle into the southwestern South Plains. Strong heating ahead of the dryline and a weak short wave trough aloft allowed scattered thunderstorms to develop across the central South Plains. A well mixed boundary layer allowed for storms to be high based and produce strong wind gusts. One Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Abernathy (Hale County) recorded severe wind gusts with the outflow well ahead of the parent thunderstorm. Weak flow allowed for storms to have little to no movement which produced heavy rainfall and flash flooding in Hockley County.
episodes.213071: Scattered thunderstorms produced heavy rain and localized flooding across northwest Indiana during the late evening of June 8th into the early morning of June 9th.
episodes.213129: During the afternoon and early evening hours of June 8th, multi-cell clusters moved over portions of west-central and south-central Illinois. These resulted in minor flooding and isolated wind damage.
episodes.213638: A few thunderstorms produced brief strong wind gusts near Chadron Nebraska.
episodes.213644: A long duration severe weather event began across southeast Wyoming during the early afternoon of June 8th and continued into the late evening hours across western Nebraska. Many strong wind gusts over 60 MPH were reported, along with large hail, flash flooding, and a tornado.
episodes.213753: Hot conditions prevailed across the Panhandles during the week of June 8 through 12. However, the combination of lingering moisture, a dryline and these hot conditions allowed for a few thunderstorms to develop each day during the afternoon and evening. Some of these storms were severe with hail and damaging winds being the main hazard.
episodes.214046: A pre-frontal trough triggered a few clusters of thunderstorms across central Illinois from the late morning through the early evening of June 9th.  Thanks to copious atmospheric moisture, one cell dropped heavy rainfall and caused localized flash flooding in parts of Fulton County.  Another storm later in the day produced damaging wind gusts and flash flooding in rural Edgar County.
episodes.214144: Two tornadoes developed on this day: an EF-1 impacting Freeland in Saginaw County and a second weak tornado near Montrose in Genesee County.
episodes.214735: A weak upper-level disturbance in combination with a very moist and unstable airmass resulted in scattered thunderstorms across northwest Tennessee. Precipitable water values over 2 inches resulted in very heavy rainfall, while SBCAPE values over 4000 J/kg provided fuel for multiple rounds of thunderstorms. Isolated flash flooding occurred in Henry County.
episodes.214838: An upper-level disturbance interacting with a surface trough triggered clusters of showers and thunderstorms across central Illinois from the late morning through the afternoon of June 8th.  With surface dewpoints in the lower to middle 70s and copious moisture within the atmospheric profile, the storms were efficient rain-producers.  There were pockets of rainfall of 1.50 to 3.00, with a few spots exceeding 4.00.  The most widespread heavy rainfall and flash flooding was focused along the I-57 corridor from Douglas County southward to Effingham County.
episodes.214960: Thunderstorms developed over northeastern Colorado during the late afternoon hours of June 8th. As this activity pushed east into southwestern Nebraska, severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts were reported. Wind gusts up to 72 MPH were reported in southwestern Hayes County.
episodes.214963: A scattered cluster of thunderstorms moved northeast across Northwest Kansas during the afternoon.  The largest hail was quarter size reported in Norton.  The highest wind gust was 65 MPH reported north of Brewster, however thunderstorm winds split a mature tree in east Graham County.  Dust storm conditions were reported in Cheyenne, Rawlins, and Thomas counties with these thunderstorms.
episodes.214965: A surface trough and low-level jet combined with a very moist and unstable air mass that led to severe thunderstorm development along the triple point of a surface low in west central North Dakota. Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon in southwest North Dakota, with additional storms in the far northwest. Storms gradually moved to the north-northeast through the evening in a primarily cluster storm mode. The area of most significant damage was in Ward and McHenry Counties. In the town of Sawyer in Ward County, the Emergency Manager reported damage from powerful thunderstorm wind gusts that resulted in power outages, trees on roads, and a large tree that fell onto a house and made a hole in the roof. Northeast of Deering in McHenry County, there was significant damage to a homestead due to thunderstorm wind gusts. A barn on the property had roof panels ripped off and some collapse of the wood frame structure for the roof. Damage in both of these locations were consistent with wind speeds around 90 mph. The largest reported hail was 3 inches in diameter, a few miles west of Fortuna in Divide County. One tornado occurred with these storms, and was reported approximately 3 miles east of Noonan in Divide County. It was a very brief tornado and caused no known damage, so has been rated EF-Unknown by NWS policy.
episodes.215151: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a sharp dryline from the late afternoon through the late evening hours on the 8th across portions of east-central and northeast Colorado. Storm motions were mostly to the east. Up to four inch diameter hail occurred in Kit Carson county, and winds up to 69 mph occurred in Yuma county.
episodes.215163: A complex of thunderstorms developed across portions of north-central Kansas during the late afternoon hours of June 8th. These thunderstorms rapidly intensified and moved south and southeast across the I-70 corridor. Widespread wind damage occurred across portions of Lincoln, Ellsworth, Saline, McPherson, Marion, and Chase counties. In fact, a wind gust of 113 mph was measured at the Salina Airport.
episodes.215179: An isolated severe thunderstorm moved north into far southwest Nebraska during the early evening hours on the 8th. Hail up to half-dollar size was reported in Dundy county before the thunderstorm rapidly dissipated.
episodes.215344: As southwest winds brought warm temperatures and moisture to the region, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed and worked east through the Lower Ohio Valley, resulting in isolated flash flooding in southern Indiana.
episodes.215347: As southwest winds brought warm temperatures and moisture to the region, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed and worked east through the Lower Ohio Valley, resulting in flash flooding and a single report of wind damage across central Kentucky.
episodes.215644: Severe Weather outbreak in southeast Idaho.
episodes.215731: A warm front moved through Central New York late in the daytime hours. This front provided enough lift to support isolated thunderstorms in a slightly unstable environment. One storm had strong gusts that resulted in several trees and wires down throughout the Hornell area.
episodes.215832: A waterspout developed off of the southeast Martin County Coast near Jupiter Island.
episodes.215847: Storms produced some damage and one tornado in west Michigan on June 9 2026.
episodes.215926: Showers and thunderstorms off the coast of South Florida produced waterspout and funnel cloud activity on the afternoon of June 9, 2026.
episodes.216019: During the early morning hours of June 9th, storms brought severe weather to portions of eastern KS.
episodes.216030: Waterspouts were observed in association with a convective cloud line north of the Lower Florida Keys.  A tropical wave was passing in the western Caribbean south of Cuba at the time.

The tornado did damage to mobile homes and tree limbs on its short path.  This was associated with a bow echo that produced widespread damage throughout northeast Kansas this night.
